facts.statement: Cacibupteryx is a rhamphorhynchid pterosaur from the Upper Jurassic Jagua Formation of Pinar del Río, Cuba.
facts.quote: Cacibupteryx is a genus of rhamphorhynchid pterosaur from the middle-late Oxfordian-age Upper Jurassic Jagua Formation of Pinar del Río, Cuba.

facts.statement: The genus Cacibupteryx was named in 2004 by Zulma Gasparini, Marta Fernández, and Marcelo de la Fuente.
facts.quote: The genus was named in 2004 by Zulma Gasparini, Marta Fernández and Marcelo de la Fuente.

facts.statement: The genus name combines the Taíno word Cacibu, meaning "Lord of the Sky", with the Greek word pteryx, meaning "wing".
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from Cacibu, the "Lord of the Sky" in Taíno and Greek pteryx, "wing".

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Cacibupteryx caribensis.
facts.quote: The type species is Cacibupteryx caribensis.

facts.statement: The genus is based on holotype IGO-V 208, which includes a partial skull missing the snout tip, teeth, and lower jaws, plus fragmentary left wing bones.
facts.quote: The genus is based on holotype IGO-V 208, a partial but well-preserved uncrushed skull — missing the tip of the snout, teeth, and lower jaws — and fragmentary left wing: the distal end of the ulna, fragments of the radius, and the first and fourth phalanx of the wing finger.

facts.statement: Describers indicated that Cacibupteryx was a relatively large form, though they did not estimate its wingspan or total length.
facts.quote: The wingspan and length were not estimated by the describers, but it was indicated to be a relatively large form.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Cacibupteryx in the subfamily Rhamphorhynchinae, closely related to Rhamphorhynchus and Nesodactylus.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses have found it to be a member of the subfamily Rhamphorhynchinae, closely related to Rhamphorhynchus and Nesodactylus.

facts.statement: Cacibupteryx lived from the Oxfordian to the Tithonian stages, between 161.5 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Tithonian (161.5 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: While recent revisions support Cacibupteryx as a basal rhamphorhynchid, researcher David Unwin suggests it may belong to the subfamily Scaphognathinae, known for robust jaws.
facts.quote: Revisiones recientes apoyan la asignación del género como un "ranforrincoide" (es decir, un pterosaurio basal), y el investigador David Unwin sugiere que era un miembro de los Scaphognathinae, una subfamilia de ranforrínquidos caracterizados por sus mandíbulas más robustas.

rejected.statement: The partial skull is 17 centimeters long, preserved in three dimensions, and features a broad roof.
rejected.quote: The partial skull is seventeen centimeters long (6.7 inches), is preserved in three dimensions, and has a broad roof.
